title: The Afternoon Brief: Russia bans Moscow mining through 2032; Senate Democrats challenge Trump's bank
dek: Russia banned bitcoin mining across Moscow and surrounding regions through 2032, citing power grid strain and cutting 16.4% of global hash power from one jurisdiction. Meanwhile, Senate Democrats introduced legislation to bar sitting presidents from owning banks, in direct response to the World Liberty Financial charter approval.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Two policy moves separated by geography and arena, one operational, one legislative, signal how crypto's scale is triggering defensive regulatory responses: Moscow's mining ban cuts capacity where it already exists; the U.S. Senate bill attempts to prevent presidential ownership before it becomes standard practice.
bottom_line: Russia's mining ban removes 16.4% of global hash power from one jurisdiction through 2032, and the Senate's bill to bar presidential bank ownership targets the emerging overlap between presidential politics and crypto infrastructure. Separately, institutional bitcoin positioning diverged: Tudor bought, UBS shifted toward calls. The desk's boards show bitcoin under selling pressure, with whales moving coins onto exchanges and ETF flows negative for three days. Watch for Wednesday's White House meeting with crypto CEOs, Thursday's CFTC Innovation Advisory Committee inaugural session, and any procedural movement on the Senate's CLARITY Act or the new presidential-banking bill; the decisive frame is whether regulatory friction accelerates or the White House engagement dampens legislative opposition.
body: Washington and Moscow sent opposing signals on crypto policy today, even as both drew from the same root: the sector's growing institutional footprint has begun to clash with established governance structures. In Russia, government decree No. 936, signed July 25 and published July 31, banned cryptocurrency mining and pool participation in Moscow, the Moscow Region, and parts of Kursk through December 31, 2032. Per the desk's reporting, Russia accounts for 175 exahashes per second, or 16.4% of global bitcoin hash power as of Q1 2026, placing it second only to the United States. Mining currently consumes roughly 1 gigawatt in the Moscow power system, and the region's data-center capacity could reach 3.6 gigawatts, or 17% of peak demand, by 2032, according to the decree. The measure directly cuts mining capacity in the world's second-largest bitcoin mining jurisdiction and signals how power-grid strain can override recent legalization.

In Washington, Senate Banking Committee Democrats led by Elizabeth Warren introduced the Ending Presidential Corruption in Banking Act on August 15 in response to the OCC's approval of World Liberty Financial's national bank charter application on January 5, 2026. The bill would prohibit sitting Presidents, Vice Presidents, their immediate families, and senior government officials from owning or controlling banks. According to Senator Warren, the reporting states, President Trump is now the first President in history to approve, operate, and supervise his own bank. The measure represents a direct legislative response to what Democrats characterize as an unprecedented conflict of interest, though the desk's reporting notes the bill's passage prospects depend on Republican Senate cooperation, which has not been detailed.

These moves occur against a backdrop of institutional capital consolidation and regulatory tightening. The desk's reporting shows that crypto startups raised $11.2 billion in the first half of 2026 across 377 disclosed rounds, with zero dollars flowing to permissionless, ungoverned projects. All disclosed institutional capital moved to regulated businesses: payments and stablecoins captured $3.7 billion, prediction markets $2 billion, and trading platforms $1.7 billion. Separately, institutional bitcoin positioning showed divergent moves. Tudor Investment raised its IBIT holdings by 18.9% to 688,529 shares in Q2 2026, ending 12 months of consecutive quarterly cuts, though the position remains 91.4% below its late-2024 peak of 8.05 million shares. UBS, meanwhile, increased call option exposure on IBIT to 1.95 million underlying shares in Q2, a 24-fold jump from 80,000 shares in Q1, while trimming direct holdings from 548,614 shares at end-2025 to 407,890 shares by June 30, a shift toward leveraged conviction rather than outright long positioning.

On the tape, the desk's Whale Watch board shows $62.6 million in net bitcoin moving onto exchanges over the past 48 hours, with the largest move into Coinbase. Bitcoin ETF flows have posted outflows for three consecutive days through August 14, totaling $385.2 million over the past five sessions. Bitcoin trades at $63,087, down 1.87% on the week and 49.4% below its 12-month high of $124,740, while the Fear and Greed Index sits at 34 (Fear), in the 30-day range of 25 to 34. The desk's boards show BTC RSI at 43.6, MACD below signal, and price below the 200-day simple moving average, consistent with the cautious risk posture that outflows and whale movement reflect.
